chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn (al-Husayn) from Abū Baṣīr from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) who said:
Verily Allah created with His hand a paradise that no eye has seen (other than Him), and no creature is familiar with.
The Blessed and Exalted Lord opens it up every morning and says, ‘Increase in [your sweet smelling] fragrance, increase in [your fresh] breeze!’
So it says (or He says), ‘Successful indeed are the believers.’
That is the [interpretation of the] verse wherein Allah, the Exalted, says: No soul can imagine what delights are hidden in store for them as a reward for what they used to do (Q32:17).
ai.seo_question: What is the unseen paradise created by Allah's hand mentioned in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Kitab al-Zuhd*, this tradition highlights the concept of *Jannat al-Kamal* (Paradise of Perfection), a unique realm created by Allah's direct hand, distinct from the physical gardens known to creation. The morning opening of this paradise symbolizes the continuous renewal of divine grace, linking the believers' ultimate success to the Quranic promise of 'hidden delights' that transcend human imagination. This reflects the Shia emphasis on the esoteric depth of reward, where the true nature of bliss is reserved for those who attain spiritual proximity to the Divine.
